title: WebMCP
description: Forms rendered with webmcp_form() and the collections listed here become callable by a browser AI agent inside the visitor's own session. Experimental: Chrome 149+ with the origin trial, and the spec is still moving.

declarativeForms.label: Agent-callable forms
declarativeForms.help: Annotate forms rendered with webmcp_form() so an agent can fill and submit them. Off, the same templates render plain forms.

readTools.label: Read tools
readTools.help: Register search_content and get_content tools over the collections below, so an agent on the page can look content up.

readCollections.label: Collections exposed as read tools
readCollections.help: A visitor's agent sees only those that allow public read (Collection → Public Operations); yours, while signed in, sees them all. Responses are marked untrusted content for the agent.

adminTools.label: Read tools in the admin dashboard
adminTools.help: Also load the read tools on dashboard pages, for an agent in your own browser. Forms in the admin are never annotated. Off by default.

maxResults.label: Search results per call
maxResults.help: The most objects a search tool returns to the agent in one call.

originTrialToken.label: Chrome origin-trial token
originTrialToken.help: Register this site's origin for the WebMCP origin trial at developer.chrome.com/origintrials and paste the token. It is emitted as a meta tag so visitors on Chrome 149+ get the API without a flag. Leave empty while testing with chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing.
